def test_move_one_ball():
    # Empty array should return True
    assert move_one_ball([]) == True

    # Single element arrays are trivially sorted
    assert move_one_ball([1]) == True
    assert move_one_ball([7]) == True

    # Already sorted arrays
    assert move_one_ball([1, 2, 3, 4, 5]) == True
    assert move_one_ball([1, 1, 2, 2]) == True

    # Arrays sortable by right shift rotation
    assert move_one_ball([3, 4, 5, 1, 2]) == True
    assert move_one_ball([2, 3, 1]) == True
    assert move_one_ball([2, 1]) == True
    assert move_one_ball([2, 2, 1]) == True

    # Arrays not sortable by any rotation
    assert move_one_ball([3, 5, 4, 1, 2]) == False
    assert move_one_ball([5, 4, 3, 2, 1]) == False
    assert move_one_ball([1, 3, 2]) == False
    assert move_one_ball([1, 2, 3, 3, 2]) == False

    # Works with negative numbers
    assert move_one_ball([-1, 0, -3]) == True   # rotates to [-3, -1, 0]
    assert move_one_ball([-5, -3, -4]) == False

    # Original array must not be modified
    arr = [3, 4, 5, 1, 2]
    move_one_ball(arr)
    assert arr == [3, 4, 5, 1, 2]
